name: t23-g3-retry-exhaustion
description: T23 / G3 row 10 follow-up. t23-g3-impaired-join.json already proves the 'bounded explicit failure' half of row 10 for a late joiner that never gets a baseline at all (its connect is delayed past server shutdown). This exercises the other half docs/reports/G3.md's post-merge review flagged as missing: retry/catch-up exhaustion while connected clients stay active -- and in doing so found a genuine, currently-unfixed gap, not just a missing test. Clients 0-2 connect live and commit 24 scripted single-cell cuts spread over ~3 s, round-robined among themselves only (client 3 owns none, so its own fate cannot change whether the required transaction count lands). Client 3 connects immediately as a --late-join replica with a shaped proxy and catch_up_cap=1; the SERVER SIDE of this works exactly as designed and is proven here: its catch-up queue overflows repeatedly as clients 0-2 keep committing (LateJoin::fan_out_transaction's existing recapture-on-overflow path), and once max_join_retries is exceeded the server correctly counts it (ServeSummary.late_join_retries / late_joins_failed) and sends Outbound::Shutdown. KNOWN GAP (not fixed here): the disconnected CLIENT does not currently turn that into the bounded 'join-failed' exit late_join_may_fail expects -- Outbound::Shutdown's Bye reason is always the generic 'server complete' whether the run ended normally or the client's retries were exhausted, and spall_net::conn's control-stream reader discards a received Bye's reason entirely (`NetMessage::Bye { .. } => return Ok(None)`), so there is currently no wire-level signal a client could act on even if it looked. The client's own late-join 'progressed' check (`config.late_join && baseline_bricks > 0`) is also too lenient here: it is satisfied by the FIRST baseline the client installed before catch-up drama began, so the client reports `result: "passed"` with a stale, non-converged hash instead of failing explicitly -- this session therefore correctly reports FAILED (a hash mismatch), which is the honest, expected outcome until that gap is fixed, not a fixture bug. Do not read a passing run of this scenario as proof retry/catch-up exhaustion is handled; read `server.summary.json`'s `late_join_retries` / `late_joins_failed` (non-zero here) as proof the SERVER half already is.
